Good morning, and welcome to the store. This week every coat and every pair of jeans is on sale, so this is a very good week for a bargain. If something does not fit, you can bring it back within thirty days. Please keep the tag on the item, and bring the receipt with you: that is our return policy. Without the receipt we can only offer you an exchange, never a refund. If an item is faulty, come straight to the counter on the ground floor, and we will change it for you on the same day. Thank you for shopping with us, and enjoy your morning.

Yesterday I found a leather bag at the market, and the price on the tag was sixty euros. That was too much for me, so I looked at the man and I asked him: how about forty? He laughed and he said fifty. Then I said: what about forty-five, and I take two of them? He thought about it for a second, and he said yes. That was a real bargain. Later I went back to the clothes store, because the shirt I bought for my wife was the wrong size. The woman at the counter looked at my receipt and asked me one question: a refund, or an exchange? I chose the exchange, and I did all of it in English.

First, Roberto sees a leather bag at the market and looks at the price on the tag. Then he makes an offer: how about forty euros? Next, the seller says fifty, and Roberto suggests forty-five for two bags. After that, the seller shakes his hand and Roberto walks away with a real bargain. Finally, he goes back to the clothes store with the receipt, and he exchanges the shirt for a larger size.
